claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion
claims.label: Anthrobots and Xenobots share similar movement types and transition profiles
claims.statement: Anthrobots and Xenobots both show discrete movement types with very low interconversion between linear and circular motion (0.2% and 0.3% for Anthrobots, 0.5% and 1.6% for Xenobots) and highly consistent circular behaviour (92% and 95%), though Anthrobot linear behaviour is more consistent (80% versus 67%).

operationalizations.text: Recompute identically defined transition matrices for Anthrobot and Xenobot trajectories and compare linear-circular conversion and state-persistence estimates with uncertainty.

Recompute, from public Xenobot tracks and from Anthrobot tracks if released, the self-transition rates of circular and linear segments and the cross-transition rates between them. Overlapping very low linear-circular exchange and circular consistency near the reported 92–95% would support the shared profile; Xenobot rates far from 0.5–1.6% and 95%, once the same indices are used, would refute the Xenobot half.

obstacles: Cross-study recording and preprocessing may differ.
Raw trajectories for both platforms may not be jointly public.
Anthrobot segment labels are not in that repository.
Straightness and gyration as defined for Anthrobots may not match the Xenobot behavior features.
Similar transition percentages do not show that the two platforms share a mechanism.

roles: public Anthrobot values and citations to the Xenobot trajectory analysis

claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric control: a mechanism for scaling cell behaviors to large-scale morphogenetic goals
claims.label: Reproducing face bioelectric patterns via ion-channel misexpression induces ectopic eyes
claims.statement: The vertebrate face is patterned by bioelectric gradients that regionalize gene expression, and reproducing these voltage patterns elsewhere in a tadpole by misexpressing specific ion channels induces whole ectopic organs such as eyes on the gut or tail, regions not otherwise competent to make eyes in response to Pax6.

operationalizations.text: Analyze voltage maps, ion-channel constructs, ectopic-eye incidence and location, and regional gene-expression responses in treated and control tadpoles. Voltage-matched manipulations using distinct channels should induce eyes outside Pax6-competent anterior tissue, whereas voltage-failing controls should not.

In Xenopus tadpoles, compare eye formation after misexpression of the specified ion channels that reproduce a facial voltage pattern in gut or tail, against the same sites after Pax6 delivery alone. Ectopic eyes at those sites after the voltage manipulation, and not after Pax6 there, would support the report; no ectopic eyes, or eyes induced equally by Pax6 outside the anterior neurectoderm, would refute it.

obstacles: Raw voltage and morphology data may not be jointly deposited.
Ion-channel misexpression has effects beyond voltage.
Eye identity and functional completeness require multiple readouts.
The induction frequencies and voltage images are in the original papers' figures, not a public animal-level file.
Injected cells can recruit neighbours, so the competent tissue is not cleanly the injected territory alone.

claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity
claims.label: Xenobots perform kinematic self-replication not known in any other species
claims.statement: Xenobots, proto-organisms that form spontaneously from dissociated frog embryo skin cells, are motile via cilia and perform kinematic self-replication, building copies of themselves from loose cells in the medium, a novel solution reached within 48 h without any evolutionary history of selection as Xenobots.

operationalizations.text: From public videos and counts, quantify whether parent Xenobots aggregate loose cells into viable motile offspring within 48 hours, while separately reviewing known reproductive modes for an equivalent process.

From the published movies and counts, score whether motile Xenopus ectoderm spheroids gather loose cells into piles that compact into further motile spheroids, and record the time from assembly to the first offspring. Offspring that swim and themselves pile cells would support kinematic replication on the reported timescale; piles that never become autonomous movers, or a requirement for a long selection history, would weaken it. A survey of other species is a separate test and is not in this archive.

obstacles: Demonstrating absence from every other species is an open-ended literature claim.
Selected videos may not represent all trials.
The public code re-runs the design simulation; it does not replace the Petri-dish counts.
Pile formation can be passive flow-driven aggregation rather than construction of a copy.
No public survey tests the claim that no other species uses this mode.

roles: public simulation and design code for the kinematic-replication model, not the wet-lab cell tracks

claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › An evolutionary intelligence ratchet
claims.label: The competency ratchet predicts no planarian mutant strains with abnormal morphology
claims.statement: The competency-ratchet model predicts, and it is the case, that there are no known mutant planarian strains with abnormal morphologies (unlike flies or mice), explains the difficulty of making transgenic planaria, and the only known permanent abnormal planarian lines (two-headed and randomized 1- vs 2-head forms) arose from bioelectric rather than genetic change.

operationalizations.text: Systematically search planarian strain, mutant, and transgenesis records for heritable abnormal morphology, classify genetic versus physiological origins, and compare discovery effort with established model organisms. A verified genetic strain with stable abnormal morphology refutes the absolute prediction.

Search FlyBase, Mouse Genome Informatics, and the planarian literature for stable inherited strains whose anatomy differs from wild type in the absence of ongoing RNAi or drug treatment. Morphological mutant strains in flies and mice, and at least one published planarian strain of that kind, would refute the negative planarian clause; a documented absence of such planarian strains, with the only permanent abnormal lines being the bioelectric one-head and two-head forms, would support it as a statement about the public record.

obstacles: Absence of reports is not proof of absence.
Planarian research effort and genetic tools differ from fly and mouse.
The claimed explanation is not uniquely predicted by the observation.
RNAi phenotypes and transient drug phenotypes are easy to mistake for mutant strains.
A literature search can refute the negative claim by finding a strain, but cannot prove that no unpublished strain exists.
Transgenesis attempts after the paper's publication can change the public record without a single dedicated database.

roles: public bibliographic database for a systematic census of mutant and transgenic planarian reports
index of planarian genetics papers through which a stable morphological mutant strain would be found

claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Beyond standard model organisms: stories of plasticity and change
claims.label: Physarum learns and decides without neurons, and its behaviour is its morphological change
claims.statement: The unicellular slime mould Physarum learns from repeated experience and makes decisions (e.g. growing towards the heavier of distant inert objects) without a brain, neurons or cellularization, and in Physarum behaviour is implemented as change of body shape, blurring the distinction between morphological and behavioural problems.

operationalizations.text: For repeated-stimulus assays, test persistent experience-dependent changes in response; for choice assays, quantify growth toward competing inert objects while controlling gradients and geometry. Time-lapse segmentation can determine whether locomotor decisions are implemented through changes in body morphology.

Measure habituation as reduced crossing of a noxious region after repeated exposure, recovered by a dishabituation control, and measure growth direction toward inert objects that differ in mass. Reduced withdrawal plus reliable growth toward the heavier object would support the learning and decision results; no change, or growth explained by a chemical cue correlated with mass, would count against them.

obstacles: Learning and decision-making have competing non-cognitive operationalizations.
Object-associated humidity or mechanical gradients can confound choice.
Raw trial-level data may not be public.
Raw trajectories are spread across papers and video supplements, not one archive.
Habituation protocols differ, and some replications have been disputed.
Growth toward mass can be a biomechanical taxis without a decision variable.

roles: public repository for microscopy time series and supplementary behavioural data

roles: public behavioural and imaging datasets for reanalysis

claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems
claims.label: A single ion channel can induce complete ectopic eyes where Pax6 cannot
claims.statement: In Xenopus, the action of a single ion channel can induce an eye-specific bioelectric state that creates complete eyes in gut endoderm, spinal cord and posterior tissues, locations where genetic master regulators such as Pax6 are insufficient in vertebrates; bioelectric states thus act as master regulators that evolution can exploit for modular anatomical change.

operationalizations.text: Score complete eye structures and tissue locations after ion-channel induction, Pax6 induction, and matched controls, verifying the predicted voltage state and comparing retinal differentiation and connectivity.

Score eye markers and lens or retinal histology in gut, spinal cord, and posterior tissue after misexpression of one ion channel, and run Pax6 at the same sites; the contrast holds if the channel induces complete eyes where Pax6 does not.

obstacles: Cross-study comparison with Pax6 may use different species, stages, and delivery methods.
Complete raw image sets may not be public.
Master-regulator status is broader than eye induction.
Histology and induction rates are in the papers, not a public image archive.
The Pax6 comparison comes from a separate vertebrate study, so sites and criteria are not matched in one dataset.
'Complete eye' has been scored with markers and anatomy of varying stringency.

roles: public expression datasets for eye induction and tissue identity where available

roles: open Xenopus ectopic-eye studies and supplementary images

claims.work: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns
claims.chapter: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 corrects Vmem
claims.label: Measured HCN2 hyperpolarization in vivo was about half the model's prediction
claims.statement: Hcn2 mRNA injection hyperpolarized the neural Vmem signal of Xenopus embryos by about 15 mV relative to controls, whereas the BETSE model predicted about 30 mV.

operationalizations.text: Estimate the injected-versus-control neural Vmem difference from embryo-level calibrated measurements and reproduce the matching model condition, then test whether observed and predicted effects are near 15 and 30 mV respectively.

Compare two deltas at the neural tube: simulated HCN2 (or IT) hyperpolarization versus control, and dye-calibrated in vivo hyperpolarization after Hcn2 mRNA. The discrepancy claim holds if the model delta is near 30 mV and the embryo delta near 15 mV; either number moving onto the other would refute it.

obstacles: Raw voltage measurements are not linked to an open repository.
The model side is more reproducible than the in-vivo side.
The in vivo ~15 mV comes from non-public voltage-dye images.
Dye calibration depends on a small set of whole-cell recordings.
Model millivolts move with the reconstructed cAMP and leak settings.

roles: public simulator for reproducing the approximately 30 mV model prediction

claims.work: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
claims.chapter: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Abstract
claims.label: Single adult human lung cells self-construct into motile multicellular biobots
claims.statement: A single normal human bronchial epithelial cell from adult lung, cultured in extracellular matrix for two weeks and then transferred to a low-viscosity medium, self-constructs into a multicellular, motile spheroid (an Anthrobot) without genetic editing, scaffolds or manual sculpting.

operationalizations.text: Audit time-lapse and lineage/protocol records for single seeded NHBE cells, quantifying clonal spheroid growth and subsequent cilia-driven displacement without editing, scaffolding, or sculpting.

Start from single dissociated adult normal human bronchial epithelial cells, culture them in matrix for two weeks, move the products to low-viscosity medium, and score multicellularity and motility without added genes, scaffolds or sculpting. Clonal spheroids that translocate would support the protocol result; aggregates that require many seed cells, or that remain immotile, would refute the single-cell self-construction claim.

obstacles: Complete single-cell lineage movies and all culture failures may not be public.
Matrigel is an extracellular matrix even though it is not a permanent scaffold.
The paper states that the supporting data are available from the authors on request, not in a public archive.
Supplementary videos illustrate motility; they do not show that each spheroid began as one cell.
Donor and batch replication counts are not in an open table.

claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › Abstract
claims.label: Resting potential of distant cells controls oncogene-dependent tumorigenesis
claims.statement: The resting membrane potentials of cells located at a distance from oncogene-expressing cells are critical for whether those oncogene-expressing cells go on to form tumors in vivo, as shown in Xenopus laevis tadpoles injected with human oncogenes.

operationalizations.text: Compare tumor-like-structure incidence in embryos with the same oncogene expression but remote hyperpolarizing versus matched control manipulations, verifying spatial separation and Vmem change. A reproducible incidence difference supports remote voltage causality.

Score tumor-like-structure incidence when oncogene mRNA and a hyperpolarizing reagent are placed in separate blastomeres, with voltage confirmed at the remote site. A lower incidence only when the remote site is hyperpolarized would support a long-range voltage requirement; no change, or a requirement for local voltage only, would refute it.

obstacles: Individual embryo data are not clearly deposited.
Remote channel expression may have effects not mediated solely by voltage.
Embryo-level voltage and tumor scores are not in a public file.
Blastomere separation is a fate-map proxy for distance, and mRNA injections carry nonspecific effects.

claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Experimental results on repatterning of planaria
claims.label: 22% of headless ERK-inhibited planaria spontaneously repattern weeks later
claims.statement: In Dugesia japonica made headless by transient U0126 (ERK/MAP kinase inhibitor) treatment after amputation, 22% of 181 animals followed until death showed sudden repatterning after four or more weeks without any intervention, mostly between 4 and 10 weeks, and 61% of those regained a normal single-headed morphology.

operationalizations.text: Use animal-level treatment, survival, observation-time, and morphology records to estimate the proportion repatterning after week four, its timing distribution, and the fraction returning to one head. The stated percentages are refuted if reclassification or survival-adjusted estimates materially differ.

Score each Dugesia japonica pre-tail fragment treated with 18 μM U0126 for three days, kept individually until death, for any morphology change after four weeks, and among those for return to one head. A recount near 22% of about 181 animals, mostly between four and ten weeks, with about 61% of the changers restoring one head, would confirm the report; a recount far from those fractions, or an independent cohort at the same dose with almost no late change, would refute it.

obstacles: Public animal-level records and videos are not identified in the source text.
Death and unequal follow-up can bias a simple proportion.
Morphological event classification may not have been blinded.
Animal-level weekly scores are not deposited; the public record is the summary and figure 10.
The scoring rubric counts fission and dorsal or lateral outgrowths as repatterning, and fission creates a new wound.
Headless animals cannot feed, so late change is confounded with prolonged starvation.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
roles: public data repository to locate deposited animal-level regeneration records or supplementary datasets
